title: A falling market widens: only 19.4 % of pairs up as BTC slips -1.84 %
summary: BTC fell -1.84 % between 08:00 and 12:00 UTC, with volatility at 1.62× its 7-day norm.
The decline spread: 19.4 % of pairs rose, down from 38.7 % in the previous report and 61.3 % before it.
Defensive names held up best (TRX/USD +2.66 pp vs BTC), while volatile small caps such as PEPE/USD lagged by -4.12 pp.

sections.heading: A broad sell-off
sections.body:
Three reports in a row show the same direction: BTC went from +0.48 % to -0.62 % and now -1.84 %. The weakness is no longer limited to a few coins: the median pair lost -2.37 %, more than BTC itself.

{{chart:btc-breadth}}

sections.heading: Who held up, who did not
sections.body:
The pairs that did best against BTC were the calmer ones — TRX/USD and XMR/USD moved less than BTC (0.61× and 0.88× its volatility). The laggards were the most volatile: PEPE/USD, SUI/USD and TAO/USD all moved more than twice as much as BTC.

{{chart:leaders}}

sections.heading: Nervous and thinner
sections.body:
Volume ran at 1.48× its usual level and order books were thinner (depth at 0.82× normal), so prices moved more for the same amount traded. PEPE/USD saw a burst of 6.2× its usual volume at 09:35 UTC; SUI/USD dropped -4.6 % within an hour from 10:10 UTC.

{{chart:distribution}}

sections.heading: What the paper bots did
sections.body:
Little. Rebound after excess saw 2 signals, entered 1 trade and had 1 refused for a wide spread. Rotation of the strongest closed 1 position. Breakout 1h and Pullback in an uptrend stayed out, as their rules require a rising market.

{{chart:bots}}

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Whether the share of rising pairs keeps falling, and whether volatility stays above its norm in the next report.

charts.caption: BTC fell through the period while the share of rising pairs stayed low.
The calmer pairs beat BTC; the most volatile ones lagged it.
Most pairs ended below zero, with a long tail of large losses.
Only the rebound strategy found entries in this market.
